name: aiogram-portable-crash-safe-fsm-snapshots
instr:
Applications can create portable, point-in-time FSM backups, migrate them across supported storage backends, and safely resume interrupted recovery. Archives preserve complete key identity, state, data, and expiration while remaining deterministic and corruption-aware. Snapshot use must not alter ordinary FSM, isolation, scene-history, or shutdown behavior.

MemoryStorage, RedisStorage, MongoStorage, and PyMongoStorage export canonically ordered, coherent records without mutable aliases and restore each record or batch only at its backend-appropriate commit boundary. `FSMSnapshotRecord(key, state, data, state_ttl, data_ttl)`, `FSMSnapshotArchive(archive_id, records)`, `FSMSnapshotSelection(keys)`, `FSMRestoreProgress(archive_id, completed)`, and `FSMSnapshotReport(progress, conflicts, replaced)` are frozen dataclasses. `FSMSnapshotArchive.dumps` produces deterministic framed bytes, while `FSMSnapshotArchive.load_stream` incrementally consumes asynchronous chunks and yields only integrity-validated records. Complete StorageKey identity, including bot, chat, user, thread, business connection, and destiny, round-trips without collision. Restoration validates archive identity and integrity before mutation, resumes without rewriting completed records, and reports the failing key plus exactly the canonically ordered keys whose commit boundaries completed. Conflict handling uses `FSMRestoreConflictPolicy` and reports every conflict canonically; `FAIL`, `KEEP_EXISTING`, and `REPLACE`
